intended_object: The pullback of a vector field V on F along a map f : E → F (meant for local diffeomorphisms): (f^*V)(x) = Df(x)^{-1}(V(f x)), with junk value 0 when Df(x) is not invertible (from the docstring).
explanation: The body `(fderiv 𝕜 f x).inverse (V (f x))` is exactly Df(x)^{-1}(V(f x)). `ContinuousLinearMap.inverse` gives the inverse when the derivative is a continuous linear isomorphism and 0 otherwise, which matches the junk value the docstring announces. The setting (any nontrivially normed field, any normed spaces E and F) is the natural one for this vector-space notion; the manifold analogue is a separate concept. I know of no broader Mathlib definition of the same object.
